scenes.narration: A dictionary stores pairs. A key, a colon, and a value. Curly brackets hold the pairs, with commas between them. Think of a fish market price board. code.source:
fish_price = {"pomfret": 350, "prawns": 500}
fish_price["pomfret"] = 380
del fish_price["prawns"]
print(fish_price)
print("prawns" in fish_price)

shorts.title: What is a dictionary?
shorts.script: A dictionary stores pairs. Each pair has a key and a value. Curly brackets, key, colon, value, with commas between the pairs. Think of a fish market price board. You look up the fish by name, and read the price. You never need to know the position. Dictionaries are how Python models labelled data, such as a student's name, age and marks. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Look up by name.

shorts.title: Read, add, change
shorts.script: Three actions cover most dictionary work. To read, write the dictionary, then the key in square brackets. To add, assign to a new key. To change, assign to an existing key, and the old value is replaced. Keys are unique, so there is only ever one pair for each key. Try all three with your own fish prices. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Read, add, change.

shorts.title: Check with in
shorts.hook: "The word in checks whether a key exists."
shorts.script: The word in checks whether a key exists. Is prawns in the dictionary? True or False. It only looks at keys, not values. Use it before you read a key you are not sure about. It saves your program from crashing, and it lets you print a friendly message when the key is missing. Check first, then read. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Does the key exist?

shorts.title: Key error
shorts.script: The classic dictionary bug. You ask for a key that is not there. Python says, key error, and shows the missing key on the last line. A dictionary does not guess. It does not return nothing. Check with in first. Or use the get method, which we use in the next episode. Read the missing key, and check its spelling. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Missing key.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the dictionary win the quiz?"
shorts.script: Why did the dictionary win the quiz? It knew every key to the answer. Your challenge. Make a dictionary of three drinks and their prices. Print the price of one drink. Then add a fourth drink to the dictionary, and print the whole thing. Check that the length is four. Post your drinks menu in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 33.
